Chapter 9: The Next Generation
As lawsuits dragged on and public backlash kept growing louder, the younger Sacklers found themselves facing a whole new kind of reckoning.
Imagine growing up surrounded by art, culture, and every opportunity you could wish for. For years, they'd enjoyed all the comforts and open doors that came with the family fortune—rarely stopping to wonder where it all came from.
But now, the world was asking tough questions. Friends started to keep their distance, invitations stopped coming in, and suddenly, having the Sackler name felt less like a privilege and more like a burden.
Some tried to stand by their family’s legacy, insisting that the good they'd done surely outweighed the harm. Others felt an overwhelming sense of guilt and shame, questioning if there was any way to make things right.
One young Sackler, who’d always dreamed of a career in the arts, found herself pushed out of the very community her family had helped support. She tried to explain—she hadn’t been involved in the business, she genuinely wanted to do good.
But the stigma was just too strong. That’s when it hit her: the choices one generation makes can shape the lives of the next, in ways you just can’t escape.
For some, this was a turning point—a chance to reflect. They started asking themselves, “What kind of legacy do I want to leave behind?” Could they use their resources to help those who’d been hurt? Was there a path to truly making amends?
It became clear—the Sackler story isn’t just about what happened in the past. It’s about the future: the choices this new generation will make, the lessons they’ll carry forward, and the hope for redemption.
